summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with a six-day history of nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain, unable to tolerate oral intake for three days. She has type 1 diabetes, gastroparesis, chronic pain, and borderline personality disorder. On admission, she had severe hyperglycemia (glucose 527) and hyponatremia (Na 132), both of which improved with IV insulin and fluids. Her anion gap metabolic acidosis resolved without progression to DKA. During the admission, she removed her GJ tube in protest over staff using it for medications, and after consultation, it was not replaced. She expressed homicidal ideation toward her roommate, whom she accused of sexual assault, but remained coherent and alert, opting to stay with a friend. She tolerated oral intake by morning and was discharged home on her prior medication regimen with wound care instructions for the GJ site.
problems: Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type I [juvenile type], not stated as uncontrolled
